feedback.overall:
1. Overall assessment  
Strong, credible CV for senior digital/public-sector communications roles: the experience shows clear progression, relevant scope, and solid platform/analytics depth. It reads professionally, but impact is reduced by dense repetition, limited quantified outcomes beyond one role, and a few style/consistency issues.

1. Top strengths  
- Clear leadership narrative: strong progression within NACo from coordinator to director to consultant, which supports credibility and seniority.  
- Relevant domain expertise: web modernization, governance, analytics, multimedia, and AI-enabled search are well aligned to the target positioning.  
- Good use of scale indicators: 10,000+ pages, 3.5 million annual page views, 50+ publishers, and tool stack details add substance.

1. Top improvements  
- Reduce repetition and tighten structure: “digital strategy/content operations/workflows/governance” appears frequently across sections. Consolidate overlapping sections like Core Competencies, Topline Skills, and Technical + IT.  
- Add more measurable outcomes across roles: several bullets describe responsibilities rather than results. Include metrics on engagement, efficiency, adoption, campaign performance, or cost/time savings.  
- Fix style consistency and minor writing issues: use one spelling standard for “organization-wide/organisation-wide” and one punctuation style for lists; “social, and multimedia” has an unnecessary comma; “Ranked among the top public universities…” is weak filler for Education. No major misspellings found.
feedback.intro:
Quick assessment: Strong, credible intro that clearly positions you for senior digital/public-sector roles. It’s slightly dense and overlaps with the subtitle, core competencies, and work experience, so tightening it will improve impact.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Replace “building the platforms” with a more active, executive phrasing like “leading” or “modernizing” to strengthen seniority.
- Add one concrete scale signal from recent experience, e.g. “10,000+ page websites” or “high-volume, multi-channel communications.”
- Trim the long service list so the intro reads faster; group related areas instead of naming every function.
- Suggested rewrite: Senior digital leader with 12+ years of experience leading web modernization, governance, analytics, and content operations for high-volume public-sector communications. Builds scalable editorial and platform systems that improve publishing, discovery, and audience engagement across complex, mission-driven organizations, including AI-enabled search and multimedia experiences.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “AI-enabled user experiences” overlaps with Core Competencies and Recent Projects.
- “Platforms, governance models and content operations” is close to the subtitle and topline skills.
feedback.coreCompetencies:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant themes, but this block overlaps heavily with the header and Topline Skills. It would be stronger if tightened to emphasize strategic capability areas rather than repeating phrasing used elsewhere.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Use shorter, sharper labels and make them parallel in structure; e.g. “Enterprise web modernization” instead of “Enterprise website modernization.”
- Replace broad items with more distinctive ones tied to recent senior work: “Drupal/CMS governance,” “AI search and discovery,” “Analytics and executive reporting,” “Cross-channel content operations.”
- Consider a tighter version: Enterprise web modernization • CMS governance and editorial operations • Analytics, dashboards and reporting • Cross-channel communications leadership • AI-enabled search and content discovery • Workflow automation and platform integration • Public-sector advocacy communications • Video, livestream and studio production
- Keep “public-sector” hyphenation consistent and consider “cross-channel” over “multi-channel” for a more current style.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “AI-enabled search and content experiences” and analytics/governance language repeat the header and Recent Projects.
- Multimedia/video/livestream capability also appears in Topline Skills and multiple roles.
feedback.footer:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant project snapshot, but it reads dense and repeats themes already covered in Work Experience. Tightening phrasing and adding clearer outcomes or scope will make it more distinctive and impactful.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Add dates or “Selected recent projects” framing to reinforce recency and separate this from core experience.
- Use parallel, tighter phrasing: start each item with a strong verb and reduce stacked nouns (e.g., “hybrid retrieval, vector search, and bill-level AI chat”).
- Where possible, add one concrete outcome, audience, or scale marker for each project.
- Standardize style: use consistent punctuation, hyphenation, and number formatting (“10 x 20-foot” rather than “10×20-foot” unless used consistently elsewhere).

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- AI Hybrid Search, microsite development, and advocacy video series closely overlap with current NACo bullets; this section should emphasize standout deliverables or outcomes not already stated.
- “Organization Anniversary Campaign” is the most distinct item; consider leading with it or expanding it slightly to avoid repetition.

items.title: Coleman DAVIS
items.subtitle: Digital Platform & Communications Systems Leader
items.content: Senior digital leader with 12+ years of experience building the platforms, governance models and content operations behind high-volume public-sector communications. Leads enterprise web modernization, analytics infrastructure, editorial systems, multimedia production and AI-enabled user experiences for complex, mission-driven organizations.

items.title: Email
items.content: coleman@colemanpdavis.com

items.title: Website
items.content: https://colemanpdavis.com/

items.title: Core Competencies
items.content: Enterprise website modernization • Digital governance & editorial systems • Analytics and reporting infrastructure • Multi-channel communications operations • AI-enabled search and content experiences • Workflow automation and platform integration • Advocacy and public-sector communications • Multimedia production and livestream operations

items.title: CV Footer
items.content:
### Recent Projects
**AI Hybrid Search**
Designed an AI-enabled legislative search experience combining hybrid retrieval, structured content workflows, vector search and bill-level AI chat to improve discovery of complex policy content.
**We Are Counties Microsite**
Built a Drupal 10 campaign microsite with custom navigation, interactive storytelling modules, downloadable resources and a modular structure designed for continued campaign growth.
**Organization Anniversary Campaign**
Developed a multi-part digital campaign combining editorial storytelling, archival media, web features and a 10×20-foot interactive conference display connected to the main site.
**Advocacy Video Series**
Built a recurring advocacy video program spanning editorial planning, production and distribution across website, email and social channels.

items.title: Strategic Communications Consultant
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Consult a U.S.-based national membership organization on digital strategy, campaign platforms, content operations and enterprise web improvement.
- Build and refine digital systems, workflows and analytics that support coordinated organization-wide communications.
- Develop campaign and storytelling experiences within the organization’s Drupal platform, including custom microsite structures, modular content sections and downloadable member-facing toolkits.
- Deliver CMS development, front-end implementation and technical troubleshooting for large public-facing web properties.
- Advise on governance, usability and operational best practices across web, email, social and multimedia channels.
- Lead development of an AI-enabled search initiative, shaping retrieval strategy, structured content workflows and user-facing discovery design.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, current role with clear strategic + technical scope, but it reads broad and overlaps heavily with your NACo director role and project highlights. Tighten it around consultant-level outcomes, transformation work, and what is new since returning.

Suggested edit
- Open with a sharper scope statement: “Advise NACo on digital strategy, Drupal platform enhancements, content operations, and AI-enabled discovery for enterprise communications.”
- Replace generic verbs with outcome-oriented phrasing: “Redesigned workflows and analytics to improve cross-team coordination” instead of “Build and refine digital systems…”
- Consolidate overlapping platform bullets into one: “Built Drupal campaign experiences, including microsites, modular content components, and downloadable member toolkits; provided front-end implementation and CMS troubleshooting.”
- Add measurable signals where possible: number of sites/components launched, teams supported, workflow time reduced, search accuracy gains, or engagement/performance improvements.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Governance, usability and operational best practices” repeats themes already covered in the Director role.
- AI search and microsite work also appears in Recent Projects; keep this entry focused on your consulting remit and impact.

items.title: Director of Digital Media
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led NACo’s digital communications team, overseeing the organization’s website, email, social media and video platforms, along with digital strategy, analytics, governance and budget management.
- Led the redesign and migration of NACo’s 10,000+ page website into a new Drupal platform supporting 3.5 million annual page views, 6,000+ average daily users and 50+ internal publishers.
- Directed NACo’s core digital communications channels, including email newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and social media platforms serving thousands of followers.
- Built NACo’s first broadcast-quality in-house video studio, expanding in-house capacity for advocacy programming, event production and recurring multimedia content.
- Expanded the organization’s analytics infrastructure across GA4, Microsoft Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio and BigQuery, improving reporting and strategic decision-making.
- Strengthened digital operations through clearer governance, publishing standards and cross-department planning systems.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, high-impact leadership entry with good scale metrics. It would be sharper if the opening emphasized enterprise ownership and if channel-management bullets added clearer outcomes rather than broad scope.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite the lead as: “Directed enterprise digital communications operations for NACo, overseeing web, email, social, video, analytics, governance, and budget for a national membership organization.”
- Tighten and front-load impact: “Led redesign and migration of NACo’s 10,000+ page website to Drupal, supporting 3.5M annual page views, 6,000+ daily users, and 50+ internal publishers.”
- Strengthen channel bullet with performance if available: add email open/click growth, audience growth, engagement rates, or campaign results; otherwise shorten to avoid generic scope language.
- Combine operations/analytics work into one outcomes-focused bullet: “Built analytics and governance systems across GA4, Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio, and BigQuery, improving reporting, publishing standards, and cross-department planning.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Video leadership overlaps with the earlier NACo role and Recent Projects; keep this version focused on building the in-house studio, not recurring video production.
- Governance/editorial systems also appear in the current consultant role and summary; avoid repeating “governance, workflows, best practices” without a distinct result.

items.title: Associate Communications Director
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social media and video, helping scale NACo’s editorial coordination and advocacy communications.
- Managed four recurring weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.
- Produced and expanded a weekly advocacy video update, helping establish video as a recurring policy communications channel.
- Strengthened editorial planning and coordination across communications, advocacy and program teams.
- Helped improve the consistency and effectiveness of NACo’s digital publishing workflows.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression story and good channel breadth, but this entry reads generic and overlaps heavily with the more senior NACo roles. Tighten it around execution, team coordination, and the early build-out of repeatable communications programs.

Suggested edit:
- Open with scope + function: “Managed day-to-day digital communications across NACo’s web, email, social and video channels, supporting editorial operations and advocacy messaging.”
- Replace “helping” language with direct ownership: “Managed four weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.”
- Make the video bullet more outcome-focused: “Produced and scaled a weekly advocacy video update, establishing video as a recurring policy communications channel.”
- Combine workflow/editorial bullets: “Improved cross-team editorial planning and digital publishing workflows across communications, advocacy and program teams.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Led digital communications across web, email, social media and video” is too close to the Director of Digital Media entry; use “managed day-to-day operations” instead.
- Video studio/build-out belongs to the later role, so keep this one focused on launching the recurring video series, not broader multimedia leadership.

items.title: Digital Strategy & Content Leadership
items.content:
- Enterprise digital strategy
- Editorial systems and governance
- Multi-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector and advocacy messaging
- Audience-focused content planning
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong themes, but this skills block is too generic and overlaps heavily with the header and Core Competencies. It should be tighter, more distinctive, and framed around senior-level scope rather than broad communications language.

Suggested edit:
- Replace with sharper, less repetitive phrasing:
- Enterprise digital strategy
- Editorial governance and content operations
- Cross-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector and advocacy communications
- Audience and journey-based content planning
- Consider swapping “messaging” for “communications” to sound more strategic and less tactical.
- If space allows, make one item more outcome-oriented, e.g. “Content operations for high-volume, multi-stakeholder publishing.”
- Keep this section focused on leadership capabilities; leave platform/tool specifics to the technical skills sections.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Enterprise digital strategy,” “editorial systems,” and “multi-channel communications” substantially repeat the header and Core Competencies.
- “Public-sector and advocacy messaging” also duplicates language already used in Core Competencies and multiple NACo roles.

items.title: Web Platforms & Technical Execution
items.content:
- Drupal
- WordPress
- SharePoint
- Power Pages
- CMS modernization
- HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery
- API integrations
- Workflow automation
- Airtable systems
- AI-enabled search experiences
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong category, but it reads like a raw tool dump and overlaps heavily with the “Technical + IT” section. In Topline Skills, this should emphasize higher-value, recent capabilities and group tools into concise themes.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite as outcome-oriented clusters, e.g.: “Drupal and CMS modernization • Front-end implementation (HTML, CSS, JavaScript, jQuery) • API integrations and workflow automation • SharePoint and Power Pages • Airtable-based operational systems • AI-enabled search experiences”
- Put Drupal/CMS modernization first; it aligns best with the most recent and highest-impact work.
- Replace “technical execution” jargon with clearer capability language if desired: “Web Platforms & CMS Delivery” or “Web Platforms & Digital Systems”
- If you can support it elsewhere, add scale signals indirectly through wording such as “enterprise CMS modernization” or “large-scale public-sector web platforms”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This item duplicates much of “Technical + IT”; keep Topline Skills higher-level and leave full tool inventory to that section.
- “AI-enabled search experiences” also appears in Core Competencies; keep it in one place unless it is a signature differentiator.

items.title: Analytics, Insights & Optimization
items.content:
- GA4
- Microsoft Clarity
- Looker Studio
- Power BI
- BigQuery
- KPI design
- Leadership reporting
- SEO and performance analysis
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant tools list, but it reads as a duplicate of the “Technical + IT” analytics section and misses the strategic value implied by this topline category. For a senior recent-profile CV, emphasize insight generation and decision support over listing platforms alone.

Suggested edit
- Reframe from tool inventory to capability-led phrasing, e.g.:
- Analytics strategy and reporting infrastructure
- GA4, BigQuery, Looker Studio, Power BI, Microsoft Clarity
- KPI framework design and executive dashboarding
- SEO, user behavior analysis and performance optimization
- Put the strategic items first; tools should support the story, not lead it.
- Replace “Leadership reporting” with “executive dashboarding” or “executive reporting” for sharper phrasing.
- If accurate, add one outcome-oriented modifier such as “decision-ready reporting” or “insight-driven optimization.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- This largely repeats “Core Competencies: Analytics and reporting infrastructure” and “Technical + IT: Data, Analytics & Optimization.”
- Avoid repeating the exact same tool list elsewhere; keep this section strategic and leave full platform detail to Technical + IT.

items.title: Multimedia Production & Event Delivery
items.content:
- Video production and editing
- Livestreaming
- PTZ camera systems
- Studio operations
- Hybrid and virtual event production
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong skill cluster, but it reads generic and overlaps heavily with the Core Competencies line and multiple NACo roles. Tighten it to emphasize higher-value, recent capabilities and use sharper phrasing.

Suggested edit:
- Replace with: **- Broadcast-quality video production and post-production - Livestream and hybrid event delivery - In-house studio operations and technical direction - PTZ camera and multi-camera production workflows**
- Lead with strategic/operational capabilities, not basic tasks; “technical direction” and “multi-camera workflows” sound more senior than “editing” alone.
- If you can support it elsewhere, add scope language such as “broadcast-quality” or “in-house studio buildout” to reflect the 2022–2024 role.
- Keep this section concise; let work experience carry the detail and any outcomes.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Livestreaming” / “multimedia production” already appears in Core Competencies; consider shortening one of the two sections.
- “Hybrid and virtual event production” overlaps with “event production” in Director of Digital Media, so avoid repeating the same wording verbatim.

items.title: University of Virginia
items.subtitle: Bachelor of Arts (BA), Economics & History
items.content: Ranked among the top public universities in the United States
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: The current line adds little value and reads like generic school marketing. For an experienced candidate, this education entry should be minimal and factual unless you have honors or distinctions worth adding.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the content line entirely with no body text; the degree, school, location, and dates are sufficient.
- If applicable, swap in a concrete credential instead: “Relevant coursework: …” or “Honors: …” only if genuinely strong and still relevant.
- Tighten the subtitle to “B.A., Economics and History” for cleaner formatting.
- Consider dropping dates if you want to reduce age signaling and keep focus on recent senior experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Ranked among the top public universities…” is generic and not candidate-specific, so it weakens the entry rather than strengthening it.
- Avoid adding coursework unless it clearly supports current digital strategy/communications work; otherwise it will feel disconnected from the stronger recent experience.

items.title: Web Platforms & CMS
items.content: Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid, scannable list, but it overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” in Topline Skills. Since recent experience is strongly Drupal-centered, reorder to reflect current relevance and consider trimming lower-signal items.

Suggested edit:
- Reorder by relevance/recency: **Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages** is fine if Drupal remains first; consider adding a qualifier if space allows: **Drupal (enterprise migration, microsites)**.
- If you want stronger positioning, rename the item to **CMS & Web Platforms** for cleaner phrasing.
- Consider tightening to the platforms you’ve materially used in recent roles; if GitHub Pages was minor, remove it to avoid diluting enterprise-level credibility.
- Optional rewrite: **Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages**.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This largely duplicates **Topline Skills → Web Platforms & Technical Execution**; keep the fuller version in one place and make this one shorter or remove overlapping platforms there.
- “CMS modernization” already appears elsewhere, so don’t add it here unless replacing another duplicate.

items.title: Coding & Technical Implementation
items.content: HTML5 • CSS3 • JavaScript • jQuery • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid technical breadth, but this reads as a generic keyword list and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” in Topline Skills. Make it more current and implementation-focused by emphasizing tools you actively use in recent roles.

Suggested edit
- Rename to: **Front-End & Technical Implementation**
- Tighten and modernize phrasing: **HTML/CSS • JavaScript/jQuery • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions**
- If accurate, add scope or outcomes in brief parentheticals: **Google Tag Manager (analytics/event deployment)** • **Cloudflare Workers (edge scripting/performance)** • **GitHub Actions (deployment/workflow automation)**
- Consider dropping version numbers (**HTML5, CSS3**) unless the CV uses versioning consistently elsewhere; they add little senior-level value.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- Duplicates **HTML, CSS, JavaScript, jQuery** and **API integrations** already listed under Topline Skills; keep them in one place or vary this section to highlight implementation tools only.
- **Workflow automation** appears elsewhere; avoid repeating it here unless tied specifically to **GitHub Actions**.

items.title: Automation & Workflow Systems
items.content: Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Basecamp • Slack • Teams • Trello
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid tool coverage, but this reads as a generic software list rather than evidence of workflow systems leadership. It also overlaps with “Workflow automation and platform integration” and “Airtable systems” elsewhere, so this item should be tighter and more role-relevant.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe by function, not just brand names: “Workflow automation: Airtable, Power Automate, Zapier | Work management: Jira, Asana, Trello, Basecamp | Collaboration: Slack, Teams”
- Prioritize the strongest, most relevant tools first; consider dropping one or two lower-value/general collaboration tools if space is tight.
- If format allows, add a light qualifier to show applied use: “used to build editorial workflows, approvals, intake systems and cross-team coordination.”
- Keep naming consistent with the rest of the CV; “Microsoft Teams” may read more polished than “Teams.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Airtable and workflow automation already appear in Core Competencies and Topline Skills; avoid repeating all three in the same generic way.
- Slack/Teams are common workplace tools and may add little unless grouped as collaboration platforms.

items.title: Email & Engagement Systems
items.content: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid, relevant platforms, but this item is too bare compared with the rest of the CV and misses a chance to signal level of use. Since recent roles emphasize enterprise email operations, lead with the most strategic/current tools.

Suggested edit:
- Reorder by likely relevance/scale: “Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp”
- If accurate, add scope qualifiers to show depth: “Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys (enterprise campaign automation) • Higher Logic (member email/community communications) • Mailchimp (newsletter/campaign delivery)”
- Consider tightening the title to “Email Marketing & Engagement Platforms” for clearer recruiter scanning.
- If space allows elsewhere, connect one platform to measurable use in recent roles (e.g., newsletters to tens of thousands), but don’t force metrics into this line item.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This overlaps with work-experience bullets about email newsletters and digital channels; keep this item tool-focused only, not responsibility-focused.
- “Higher Logic” may imply community platform functionality, so avoid repeating community/engagement claims unless supported elsewhere.

items.title: Data, Analytics & Optimization
items.content: GA4 • Microsoft Clarity • Looker Studio • Power BI • BigQuery • SEO • A/B testing • Dashboarding
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong tool coverage, but this item is overly generic and duplicates the “Topline Skills” analytics section almost exactly. It should either be tightened to emphasize technical tools only or reframed around applied analytics/optimization outcomes.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite as: “GA4 • BigQuery • Power BI • Looker Studio • Microsoft Clarity • SEO analysis • A/B testing • KPI dashboard development”
- Put the most credible/strategic tools first: GA4, BigQuery, Power BI, Looker Studio; move broader concepts like SEO and A/B testing later.
- Replace “Dashboarding” with “KPI dashboard development” or “executive reporting dashboards” for stronger specificity.
- If space allows elsewhere, connect these tools to outcomes in recent roles instead of listing generic capabilities here.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This is highly redundant with “Topline Skills – Analytics, Insights & Optimization”; consider deleting one section or differentiating this one as tools-only.
- “SEO” and “A/B testing” are capabilities, not platforms, so they may fit better in competencies than Technical + IT.

items.title: Work Eligibility
items.content: Full legal authorization to work in Belgium (Visa D + residence permit / carte de séjour)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Useful for Belgium-based applications, but the phrasing is a bit legalistic and takes more space than needed. This should read as a clear status note, not a headline achievement.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite for brevity and recruiter scanability: “Authorized to work in Belgium (Visa D and residence permit).”
- If accurate, make it stronger and simpler: “Fully authorized to work in Belgium; residence permit in place.”
- Avoid the French term unless the role specifically requires bilingual administrative terminology; “residence permit” is usually enough.
- Consider moving this into the contact/header area for local applications, since eligibility matters more there than in a secondary rail.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- No major duplication, but this item is lower-value than recent experience; keep it very short so it doesn’t compete for attention.
- If location/contact already signals Belgium and applications are local, this may be optional rather than essential.

items.title: Languages
items.content:
**English** (Native)
**French** (A2/Learning)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but too compressed and visually awkward. It should be reformatted for quick scanning and framed honestly so French supports your Belgium-based role without overstating proficiency.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite as a simple line: Languages: English (native) | French (A2, currently improving)
- Use lowercase proficiency style for consistency and cleaner tone: native, A2, conversational/basic if accurate.
- If relevant to target roles, add practical context only if true: French (A2, professional working improvement underway)
- Keep it concise; this section is supporting information, not a selling point versus your recent digital leadership experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- No major duplication, but avoid overdesign/bolding here; the CV already has strong skills sections competing for attention.
- If space is tight, this can stay in the rail and should not be repeated in the header, summary, or cover letter unless language is job-relevant.

items.title: Soft Skills
items.content: Cross-department coordination • Stakeholder communication • Team leadership • Strategic planning • Clear writing and editing • Problem-solving • Adaptability
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This section is too generic and largely repeats strengths already proven in the summary and core competencies. On a senior CV, “soft skills” should either be removed or reframed as leadership traits tied to scope and outcomes.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to “Leadership Strengths” or “Management & Collaboration” to sound more senior and less filler.
- Cut generic items like “Problem-solving” and “Adaptability”; keep only traits that support target roles.
- Tighten to 4–5 items max, e.g.: Cross-functional leadership • Executive stakeholder management • Editorial judgment • Team development • Strategic planning
- If space is tight, remove this section entirely and use the room for quantified achievements in recent roles.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-department coordination” and “Stakeholder communication” duplicate the header summary and Core Competencies.
- “Team leadership” and “Strategic planning” are already demonstrated more credibly in the 2022–2024 Director role.

items.title: References
items.content: References available upon request.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item adds little value and uses space that could better support recent, higher-impact experience. “References available upon request” is assumed by most employers and usually should be removed.

Suggested edit:
- Delete the “References” entry entirely.
- Use the freed space for stronger supporting content instead, such as a brief “Selected Results” rail item with 1–2 metrics from recent roles.
- If references are specifically requested, provide them separately rather than on the CV.
- If you want a replacement rail item, consider “Work Authorization” or “Languages,” which are more useful and already present here.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This section is redundant because reference availability is standard and does not differentiate you.
- Keeping it may weaken the second-page rail by displacing more relevant, recent qualifications.

items.title: Digital Media Manager / Producer
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Advanced through two digital roles, supporting the creation of the organization’s first in-house digital team and strengthening workflows across web, email, social, and multimedia. Contributed to a major website refresh and produced high-impact digital content—including livestreams and weekly video updates—while providing day-to-day guidance to a digital media associate.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid progression story, but the item is too broad and overlaps with later NACo roles on workflows, video, and team leadership. Make it more execution-focused and foundational, with concrete outputs if you can add metrics.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite to emphasize early-career build work: “Promoted across two digital roles to help launch NACo’s first in-house digital media function, supporting web, email, social and multimedia production.”
- Add specific scope/results: website refresh contribution, number/frequency of livestreams or weekly videos, audience reach, event support, or production volume.
- Tighten leadership phrasing: replace “providing day-to-day guidance” with “mentored a digital media associate” only if that supervision was meaningful.
- Possible version: “Promoted across two roles to help establish NACo’s first in-house digital media team. Supported a major website refresh and produced recurring digital content, including livestreams and weekly video updates, while improving cross-channel production workflows across web, email, social and multimedia.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Strengthening workflows” repeats language used in 2018–2024 roles.
- “Weekly video updates” overlaps with the later advocacy video bullet; distinguish this as the earlier launch/build phase.

items.title: County Solutions & Innovations Coordinator
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Coordinated innovation and research projects supporting organizational programs and policy work. Contributed to digital content production and multimedia materials, and launched the organization’s first podcast, overseeing planning, scripting, and production.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid early-career entry, but it reads generically and underplays the most distinctive achievement: launching NACo’s first podcast. Since later roles already cover broad digital/media leadership, this item should emphasize innovation support plus that first-launch accomplishment.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite to foreground the standout result: “Coordinated innovation and research initiatives supporting NACo programs and policy priorities; launched the organization’s first podcast from concept through scripting and production.”
- Replace vague phrasing like “contributed to digital content production” with more active language: “produced multimedia and digital content assets supporting program and policy communications.”
- If possible, add scope or outcome: number of episodes, audiences served, internal stakeholders supported, or how the podcast expanded communications capacity.
- Keep it to 1–2 lines; this is an older role, so concise impact matters more than full duty coverage.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Avoid repeating generic multimedia/video language already covered in later NACo roles.
- Don’t overstate digital leadership here; reserve team-building and enterprise-scale ownership for 2015–2024 roles.

items.title: Multimedia & Creative Tools
items.content: Premiere Pro • Audition • Photoshop • Illustrator • Livestream studio workflows • Podcast production
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Useful supporting skills, but this item is currently generic and overlaps heavily with “Multimedia Production & Event Delivery” in Topline Skills. Make it more software/tool-specific and trim workflow language already covered elsewhere.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite as: **Premiere Pro • Audition • Photoshop • Illustrator • Podcast recording/editing • Livestream production support**
